references.text: Moses is instructed to consecrate the people for two days before the Lord's coming on the third day, providing context for the command to be prepared.
The law regarding ritual impurity after sexual intercourse, explaining why the people were to abstain from women before their holy meeting with God.
David asks the priest for bread, and the priest replies that he can give it if the men have abstained from women—a similar requirement of sexual abstinence before a sacred act.
Paul advises married couples to abstain from sexual relations for a time to devote themselves to prayer, reflecting the principle of temporary abstinence for spiritual preparation.
Moses is told to be ready by morning and go up Mount Sinai, a similar command to prepare before meeting with God.
Joshua commands the people to consecrate themselves because the Lord will do wondrous things, the same principle of consecration before God's mighty acts.
Joshua instructs the people to consecrate themselves before an important event, reflecting the requirement for preparation in Exodus 19:15.
Both texts establish boundaries for consecration where humans must keep their distance due to God's holy presence.
